ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure is a schematic diagram of transistor output characteristics/DC load line, with the vertical axis as Ic(mA) and the horizontal axis as VCE(V). A DC load line sloping downward to the right intersects the characteristic curve labeled Ib = 40 μA at the operating point Q. Along the same load line, there is a point Q' to the upper left of Q, indicating larger Ic and smaller VCE; there is a point Q'' to the lower right of Q, indicating smaller Ic and larger VCE. Reasoning: The problem states that it is a fixed-bias single-transistor AC amplifier circuit. Under fixed bias, an increase in temperature will make the transistor collector current Ic increase. Since the operating point is still constrained by the same DC load line, when Ic increases, VCE will decrease, so point Q should move along the load line toward the upper left, that is, toward Q'.

raw_record.question_text: In the circuit shown in the figure, for a fixed-bias single-transistor AC amplifier circuit, when the temperature increases, toward which point will the operating point \(Q\) move?

method.method_draft: Identify Q on the plotted load line. From the text, note that the amplifier is fixed-bias and temperature is increasing. Apply the BJT temperature rule that Ic increases under fixed bias. On the graph, move from Q to the point with higher Ic and lower VCE along the same load line; this is the point labeled Q'. Therefore the operating point moves toward Q'.

method.method_draft: Read the text to classify the amplifier as fixed-bias. Recall that fixed bias has poor thermal stability: temperature rise drives the transistor toward larger collector current and closer to saturation. Compare the labeled alternatives in the figure: the saturation/high-current direction from Q is up-left, where Q' is located; Q'' is down-right and would correspond to reduced collector current/cutoff direction. Therefore choose movement toward Q'.
